title: Redwood discovery with Fortress Capital
summary: Discovery focused on cost/unit economics across Redwood Hosted, Dedicated and Private. Customer budget constraints, latency targets, and security requirements discussed. Agreed next steps: run a benchmark with their 3 representative prompts, share detailed pricing and security pack, schedule Dedicated sizing call.
next_steps: Redwood to run pilot benchmark on Fortress sample prompts (SE) - due 2027-01-06
Send pricing sheet and hosted vs dedicated TCO scenarios - AE (Sophie) - due 2026-12-31
Share SOC2 and network architecture docs - SE (Marco) - due 2026-12-31
Schedule Dedicated sizing deep-dive - calendar invite from Sophie - due 2027-01-04
action_items: Marco Alvarez - run 3-prompt latency/cost benchmark on both hosted and dedicated configs - 2027-01-06
Sophie Lin - send hosted vs dedicated TCO scenarios and sample contract language - 2026-12-31
Aisha Khan - provide 3 representative prompt sets and peak QPS expectations - 2026-12-30
transcript:
[00:00] Sophie Lin: hey everyone thanks for joining from Redwood. quick intros, i'm Sophie, AE. Marco with me is our SE.
[00:10] Marco Alvarez: hey hi, thanks. happy to dig into the cost side and the benchmark.
[00:18] Clara Meyer: thanks, we're excited. i'm Clara, CTO at Fortress. we'll primarily care about unit economics and the security side.
[00:27] Aisha Khan: hi all, Aisha here, head of ML. we run a few LLM features in prod — classification, summarization and a Q/A over internal docs.
[00:35] Ben Rhodes: Ben — infra. i'll ask the VPC and throughput questions.
[00:40] Marco Alvarez: great. agenda — we want to understand your current stack, target latency and budget, then talk about Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private and how batching/caching affect per-token costs.
[00:51] Sophie Lin: just to set context, many customers start hosted then move to Dedicated as they scale because of predictable throughput and better unit economics, but private deployments are typical for regulated data.
[01:05] Aisha Khan: our initial constraint is budget. we estimate about $20k/month for LLM infra right now for PoC, with potential to scale to $80k/month if latency and quality are good.
[01:16] SOPHIE (note: auto-label): got it. what's your current cost per inference?
[01:20] Aisha Khan: hard to say, we pay per token on our current vendor, roughly $0.0008/token for some models but that's variable. our concern is unpredictable cost spikes from long contexts and chaty sessions.
[01:34] Marco Alvarez: right — so two levers to control cost: batching (throughput improvements) and KV/prefix caching which reduces repeated token compute for conversations. with Redwood we can suggest batching windows and prefix caching policies that often cut token compute by 20-60% depending on reuse.
[01:52] Ben Rhodes: curious — how much of that is achievable on hosted vs dedicated?
[01:57] Marco Alvarez: hosted supports all our caching/batching features; however Dedicated gives you more control over autoscaling and sustained throughput which tends to lower effective cost per token at scale because you avoid per-request overhead and get predictable slot pricing.
[02:11] Clara Meyer: can you quantify? give me an example per-token comparison at different loads.
[02:17] Marco Alvarez: yes, rough example — for a 13B model on hosted, our list price might be $0.0006/token for generation (this is illustrative) whereas Dedicated reserved capacity amortized could bring effective cost to $0.00025-$0.0004/token depending on utilization and batching. the delta is mostly from reserved GPU amortization and continuous batching.
[02:37] Aisha Khan: that's a big difference. but we're worried about upfront commit risk. what kind of minimums for Dedicated?
[02:44] Sophie Lin: Dedicated typically has monthly committed throughput commitments; we structure tiers. smallest Dedicated starts around equivalent to a few VMs/GPU-hour allocation; we'll tailor based on your peak QPS and desired SLOs. we'll map that to monthly cost.
[02:58] Ben Rhodes: on the Private side — we need VPC peering and our KMS, plus audit logs. is that supported?
[03:05] Marco Alvarez: yes — Private allows customer-managed KMS and VPC endpoints, audit logs shipped to your SIEM. our Private package also includes on-prem options if you need air-gapped.
[03:16] David Yu: how about data retention? some of our workflows require short retention and strict deletion.
[03:21] Marco Alvarez: retention policies are configurable; for Hosted we have contractual options for retention windows and can disable retention for certain routes; Dedicated and Private give you more control and logs remain within your network if Private.
[03:34] Aisha Khan: back to batching — do we need to change prompts or client logic?
[03:39] Marco Alvarez: minimal changes; batching is done at the runtime. there are knobs — preferred batch window and max latency. for low-latency routes we keep small batch windows; for async jobs you can batch longer to increase throughput.
[03:52] Sophie Lin: also KV/prefix caching — if you're doing chat over same doc set we can cache embeddings/keys so repeated tokens don't re-run full attention. that helps a lot with cost on multi-turn.
[04:04] Clara Meyer: what's the typical ROI on caching? any numbers?
[04:09] Marco Alvarez: depends on reuse patterns. for heavy multi-turn agent workflows, we've seen 40-60% compute reduction. for single-shot classification, caching isn't helpful.
[04:21] Ben Rhodes: for our estimate, we have three workloads: real-time Q/A peak 50 qps, async bulk summarization 5k docs/day, and a chat assistant with average 6 turns.
[04:34] Sophie Lin: perfect. those map to different configs. real-time Q/A needs low latency SLO (under 150 ms token latency if possible), so batching window must be small, you get less batching gains but Dedicated may help. async jobs are where you can schedule big batches and use quantized models to cut cost.
[04:51] Aisha Khan: quantization — how much does that affect quality vs cost?
[04:55] Marco Alvarez: quantization (8-bit/4-bit) often reduces GPU memory and can increase throughput; quality drop is model-dependent. we recommend evals on your prompts; often 8-bit has near-identical quality, 4-bit needs testing. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization profiles per workload.
[05:12] Sophie Lin: can we talk about sample numbers: if your PoC budget is $20k/month, we can propose a hosted pilot with strict quota and caching rules to keep costs predictable, and run a benchmark to estimate Dedicated break-even.
[05:26] Clara Meyer: what's the ballpark break-even you see?
[05:29] Marco Alvarez: rough rule — if you're sustaining >>50M tokens/month with good batching/utilization, Dedicated becomes compelling; below that hosted often is simpler. exact numbers depend on model size and utilization.
[05:44] Ben Rhodes: 50M tokens sounds like a lot, can you translate to QPS for our workloads?
[05:49] Marco Alvarez: for small outputs, say average 50 tokens/generation, 50M tokens/month is about 1M generations/month ~ 12 gen/sec sustained — very workload dependent.
[06:02] Aisha Khan: ok. we'll provide our sample prompts and we want you to run a benchmark on both hosted and Dedicated with our 3 workloads.
[06:10] Marco Alvarez: absolutely, we'll run latency and cost per-token measurements and include caching/batching knobs.
[06:15] Sophie Lin: we'll need your sample prompts, expected QPS windows, and any throughput bursts. also clarify retention and security needs.
[06:23] David Yu: security — SOC 2, SSO and RBAC are table stakes for us. do you support SCIM and SAML?
[06:29] Marco Alvarez: yes. Hosted supports SAML SSO and SCIM; Dedicated includes integration into your enterprise IAM and Private gives full network isolation with customer KMS. we will attach SOC2 and ISO docs; for Dedicated/Private we can do more granular RBAC.
[06:43] Ben Rhodes: network egress — if hosted, is there option for VPC egress to our cloud?
[06:49] Marco Alvarez: we have VPC peering options and egress controls on some hosted tiers; for strict network controls Dedicated or Private is recommended.
[06:58] Sophie Lin: any concerns on pricing transparency? customers worry about hidden costs like context window length and long-running sessions.
[07:06] Aisha Khan: yes, unpredictable long sessions are our biggest fear.
[07:09] Marco Alvarez: we do per-token metering with route-level quotas and alerts; you can set max tokens per session and per-route budgets. we'll show you how to set budget alarms.
[07:20] Clara Meyer: how do you handle fallback when capacity is constrained? we don't want errors in prod.
[07:26] Marco Alvarez: Redwood supports smart routing/fallback policies — fallback to smaller model variants or to queued mode. also can stitch multiple model variants to preserve availability. Dedicated helps because reserved capacity reduces fallback events.
[07:40] Aisha Khan: about benchmarks — what metrics will you provide?
[07:43] Marco Alvarez: we'll provide p50/p90/p99 token latency, overall throughput, cost per generated token, GPU utilization, and effective tokens saved due to caching.
[07:54] Sophie Lin: timeline wise, Sophie: we'll share a pricing TCO doc by end of week and SE will run benchmarks early next week.
[08:01] Ben Rhodes: fine. one more — do you support private model hosting for our proprietary fine-tuned models?
[08:07] Marco Alvarez: yes — Dedicated can host your fine-tuned artifacts; Private or on-prem can keep models entirely inside your network. we also support model pinning and version rollouts.
[08:18] Clara Meyer: does Redwood do model quantization for customers or do we need to do it ourselves?
[08:22] Marco Alvarez: Redwood Optimize includes quantization recommendations and we can run quantize-and-eval as part of the benchmark engagement as a service.
[08:31] Aisha Khan: great. any notable gaps we should be aware of?
[08:35] Marco Alvarez: probably nothing blocking; we'll validate latency SLOs during the benchmark and show Dedicated sizing if utilization suggests it.
[08:42] Sophie Lin: recap — Redwood to run benchmark using customer prompts on hosted and Dedicated configs, share pricing/TCO, security docs, and schedule a Dedicated sizing call.
[08:51] David Yu: agreed. thanks.
[08:53] Sophie Lin: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with an email and next steps.
[08:58] (call ends)
questions: What is the break-even token/month threshold for Dedicated?
How much does caching reduce effective token compute for multi-turn chat?
What commit levels are required for Dedicated tiers?
notes: Customer PoC budget $20k/month, scaling to $80k+/month if results are good
Three workloads: 50 qps real-time Q/A, 5k docs/day async summarization, chat assistant avg 6 turns
Security requirements: SOC2, SAML/SCIM, KMS, VPC peering
